# RE2JS for draw.io CORS rules

Pinned upstream package: [re2js 2.9.1](https://www.npmjs.com/package/re2js/v/2.9.1), MIT. `re2js.umd.js` is the unmodified published browser build. Its SHA256 is `c826d974feef561e90d526ec78d9ac57f418040a49b7b2b5d862f69ebddd3b2f`. The complete license is in `LICENSE` and is retained in every generated bootstrap.

The `cors` URL parameter uses RE2 matching through the maintained adapter in `internal/server/web/drawio-linear-regex.js`. Rules are limited to 512 UTF-16 code units and 4096 program instructions; custom-rule match inputs are limited to 8192 UTF-16 code units. Encoded parameter input is limited before decoding. Lookaround and backreferences are unsupported and use the normal image-proxy route, as do invalid, oversized or undecodable rules. Built-in provider handling is retained; same-origin decisions compare parsed origins. There is no native backtracking fallback.

`node scripts/sync_drawio_linear_regex.cjs` generates `js/re2js-safe.min.js` and the identical guarded bootstrap in app, integrate and both viewer bundles. It also synchronizes `Editor.isCorsEnabledForUrl`. Set `AIDE_TERSER_MODULE` to a module path containing Terser 5.39.0; use `--check` to verify instead of writing. The generator rejects upstream hash changes until explicitly reviewed. The standalone script supports source/development loading; bundled exports carry their own bootstrap and need no extra network library load. The initialization guard uses a SHA256 build identity covering the engine, adapter and license, so a cached adapter with the same engine version is replaced when its policy changes. All resources are shipped locally.

`node scripts/test_drawio_cors_linear.cjs` checks native-regex compatibility for the supported URL-rule corpus, resource and syntax rejection, graceful fallback, bootstrap namespace isolation and a terminable Worker regression. The worker proves that nested-quantifier input finishes rather than blocking the calling UI; it is not a general performance guarantee for arbitrary devices.
